Andrea — thanks for the note and for flagging the VAT point. Quick options below (we’re happy to accept whichever is easiest for you, just confirm which route you’ll take):

OPTION A — EUR account (recommended to avoid correspondent routing)
- Account name: Redwood Finance Europe LTD
- IBAN: DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00
- BIC/SWIFT: MARKDEFFXXX
- Currency: EUR (credit as EUR)
- Instruction: Please include invoice ref: IN-3892 and payer VAT id.
- Benefit: avoids USD correspondent chain and reduces intermediary deductions; simpler VAT treatment for EU payers.

OPTION B — USD beneficiary account (if payer prefers to pay USD from their EUR account)
- Account name: Redwood Inference Inc.
- Account: 123456789
- SWIFT: RWINUS33XXX
- Currency expected on beneficiary: USD 43,750
- Instruction: To guarantee full USD credit, set ordering instruction to OUR (sender cover). If you select SHA, the originating bank will share intermediary charges and we may receive less than the invoiced USD amount.

Policy / fee handling
- Redwood prefers receiving the full invoiced amount. If a payment arrives short due to intermediary deduction (SHA), we will invoice the shortfall back to the payer rather than automatically absorb it.
- If you prefer, we can accept SHA and then raise a small reconciliation invoice for any intermediary deductions — please advise.

VAT / invoice modification
- For EU B2B customers (VAT-registered), Redwood can issue an updated invoice indicating reverse-charge if you confirm your VAT id. That will help your reclaim.

Practical asks
- Please confirm: (1) which account you will use (Option A or B), (2) final EUR amount to be sent (if paying from EUR), and (3) confirm you will include invoice ref IN-3892 in the payment narrative.

I’ve attached a short wire template with the fields our banks need. If you want us to absorb a single intermediary fee as a gesture, we can evaluate on a case-by-case basis — if that is required, please attach the SWIFT advice after payment so we can reconcile.

Best,
Markus Klein
